characters.name: Carl
characters.note: The cannonball man. Very round, 1.70 m, messy brown hair, big worried white eyes, orange-tan skin, red trunks with a white drawstring. No mouth. Meshy 7 mesh from the GPT Image 2.5 T-pose picked for him, about 10k tris. Rigged on Coach Panic's own 24-bone skeleton (rig_from_template.py) plus three belly bones (belly_bones.py: BellyUpper, BellyMid, BellyLower), so the stomach moves by itself: belly_jiggle.py keys it in every clip (it lags the body, bounces on steps and landings, rises with each breath in the idles). The Coach's clips retargeted onto it (retarget_clips.py, and Panic and Swim by transplant_clips.py): the same motion, hip travel x0.70, but with the arms swung out of the belly (by up to 54 degrees) and the knees' bend cut where a shin would go into it (by up to 51 degrees, a third of a run's knee) by clear_limbs.py, so the arms stay beside the body in a walk and a run (in Swim and IdleScratch a hand rests on the belly for a few frames). Feet put on the floor by ground_clips.py. Own clip Cannonball, the only character that has one (2.25 s, plays once, in place: the game moves him): a deep crouch with the arms swung back, an explosive push, the belly and chest rising first, the knees lifting only as far as the belly lets them, the feet curled underneath, elbows out and the hands round the belly's flanks, the tuck held at the top with the shoulders rounded and the head tucked, a fall at 9.8 m/s2 and a bottom-first splash into water 0.25 m below the deck at frame 37, the pose rocking back, the arms flung out, and a sink under the surface. The viewer shows it over a pool, running him off the deck.

Cannonball.why: the knees snap straight in the push-off and fold up in the tuck at about 40 degrees a frame

characters.name: Fish kid
characters.note: The kid of the Fish Kid incident: Nico's mesh (a boy of 1.2 m, spiky hair, goggles, orange armbands, no mouth) with the four clips of a boy who carries a bucket to the pool and tips it out, and a node of the skeleton, BucketMount (a child of the chest bone, not a joint), that the carrying clips move: dist/assets/bucket.glb, a Meshy 7 bucket from a GPT Image-style picture (Nano Banana Pro), hangs in it in the game, so the bucket goes where the hands go. tools/blender/carry_clips.py makes them from Nico's Walk, Run and IdleScan (the arms replaced by the same hold in every frame: the bucket at the chest, the hands on its two sides, so it sways with the body) and builds BucketDump with two-bone IK (a breath in, the bucket heaved up and out and tipped past the horizontal, a shake, and lowered): the game plays it over the second the incident takes, so the bucket is out when the fish goes in. The viewer does not show the bucket.
